name: document_validation
doc:
DOCUMENT VALIDATION - the check digits, sealed (issue #11, 2026-10-16: reach, down the domain list). Through
document_validation.DOC_VERIFY: ISBN-10 (mod 11, with the X check digit), ISBN-13 and EAN-13 / UPC-A (mod 10,
weights 1 and 3), and Luhn (payment cards and IMEI). Valid published identifiers are SEALED as valid; a
transposed ISBN-10 and a one-digit Luhn error are SEALED as invalid (claimed false); and the known blind spot of
the mod-10 code - an adjacent transposition of digits differing by 5 passes - is SEALED as the instance it is.
The code designs are CITED. Idempotent.

sticks.question: Document validation - the check digits, sealed
sticks.statement: A check digit is a theorem of modular arithmetic: the weighted sum of a valid identifier is 0 mod 11 (ISBN-10) or 0 mod 10 (ISBN-13, EAN, UPC, Luhn).
references: H. P. Luhn, US Patent 2,950,048 (1960); ISO/IEC 7812-1
GS1 General Specifications, section 7.9 (check digit calculation)
J. A. Gallian, Error detection methods, ACM Computing Surveys 28 (1996) 504

marks.claim: [an ISBN-10, SEALED] 0-306-40615-2 is valid (sealed through document_validation.DOC_VERIFY): weights 10 down to 1, sum 0 mod 11.
[the C book, SEALED] 0-13-110362-8, The C Programming Language (2nd ed.), is valid (sealed through document_validation.DOC_VERIFY): the sum is 88 = 8 x 11.

[the X, SEALED] 0-8044-2957-X is valid (sealed through document_validation.DOC_VERIFY): mod 11 has eleven residues, so one check value is 10 and is written X. The alphabet grew by one letter because the modulus is prime.

[a transposition caught, SEALED AS INVALID] 0306460152 - the 0 and 6 of 0306406152 swapped - is invalid, sealed with claimed = false (sealed through document_validation.DOC_VERIFY). Mod 11 with distinct weights catches EVERY adjacent transposition: swapping digits a and b shifts the sum by a - b, never 0 mod 11.

[an ISBN-13, SEALED] 978-0-306-40615-7 is valid (sealed through document_validation.DOC_VERIFY) - the same book as the ISBN-10 above, re-coded under the 978 prefix with a new check digit, mod 10 with weights 1 and 3.
[another, SEALED] 978-0-596-52068-7 is valid (sealed through document_validation.DOC_VERIFY): the weighted sum is 130.

[Luhn, SEALED] 79927398713 passes Luhn (sealed through document_validation.DOC_VERIFY): double every second digit from the right, subtract 9 from any double above 9, and the sum is 0 mod 10. Every payment card number ends in a Luhn digit.
[an IMEI, SEALED] 49-015420-323751-8 passes Luhn (sealed through document_validation.DOC_VERIFY): a phone's identity carries the same check as a card.

[one digit wrong, SEALED AS INVALID] 79927398714 fails, sealed with claimed = false (sealed through document_validation.DOC_VERIFY). Luhn catches every single-digit error - the doubling-and-casting-out-nines makes each position's contribution a bijection on the digits.
[an EAN-13, SEALED] 4006381333931 is valid (sealed through document_validation.DOC_VERIFY): weights 1,3,1,3,... sum 0 mod 10.

[the blind spot, SEALED] 4006831333931 - the 3 and 8 of the EAN above swapped - is ALSO valid (sealed through document_validation.DOC_VERIFY). Weights 1 and 3 differ by 2, so a swap of adjacent digits a, b shifts the sum by 2(a - b); when a - b = 5 that is 10, invisible mod 10. The code catches every single-digit error and most transpositions but not this one; the engine seals the limitation as an instance, not an exception.
[a UPC-A, SEALED] 036000291452 is valid (sealed through document_validation.DOC_VERIFY): twelve digits, read as an EAN-13 with a leading zero - the two codes are one scheme.

[the designs, CITED] ISBN-10's mod 11 (ISO 2108), the mod-10 1/3 weighting of EAN and ISBN-13 (GS1), and Luhn's doubling (1960) are chosen designs: cited as postulates. What each design DETECTS is a theorem of modular arithmetic - sealed above by instance, proven in general by Gallian (1996): a prime modulus with distinct weights catches all single errors and all adjacent transpositions; mod 10 cannot catch them all, and the 5-apart swap is the proof.
marks.source: ISO 2108:2017; GS1 General Specifications 7.9; Luhn, US 2,950,048; Gallian, ACM Comput. Surv. 28 (1996) 504

marks.claim: [on the one map] A check digit is an error-detecting code (card_floor_computer_science: parity and its generalizations), built from modular arithmetic (the number-theory floor: residues, a prime modulus) and judged by information theory (the information-theory stick: one redundant symbol buys detection, not correction). The engine never reads a card number or an identity - it checks a published example's arithmetic, nothing more.
marks.source: the one map; card_floor_computer_science; the information-theory stick
